snippet.title: The Most Valuable YouTube Lesson You'll Ever Learn
snippet.description:
Join my FREE live YouTube workshop every Sunday:
https://aimediacompanies.com/r/lesson

The most valuable YouTube lesson I've learned after building 14 channels, growing multiple channels past 1 million subscribers, and generating hundreds of millions of views is simple: never create a video without evidence that people already want to watch it.

In this video, I break down the 5-step strategy I use to find viral YouTube ideas, analyze outliers, create better titles and thumbnails, improve audience retention, and identify which videos are actually worth making.

I also share real examples from my own channel, including videos that reached 187,000 and 73,000 views, alongside videos that struggled to get even 1,000. Same creator, same editing, completely different results.

You'll see how I use data to make better decisions, why the first 30 seconds matter so much, how to attract the right audience, and why studying failed videos is just as important as studying successful ones.

Stop guessing what to upload. Start making decisions based on evidence.

snippet.title: Treat YouTube Automation Like A Video Game And Get Rich
snippet.description:
Join my FREE live YouTube workshop every Sunday:
https://aimediacompanies.com/r/levels

YouTube automation is like playing a video game. There are 6 levels, and each one has a specific skill you need to master before moving to the next.

Most beginners fail because they're trying to skip levels. They hire editors before making their first video, automate everything before understanding the algorithm, or try scaling channels that aren't making money yet.

In this video, I break down all 6 levels of faceless YouTube, from finding a profitable niche and mastering titles and thumbnails to using AI, hiring a team, and building channels that operate without your daily involvement.

I also share which levels I've personally been through, what you can realistically earn at different stages, and how to eventually turn your YouTube channels into valuable digital assets that can generate income and potentially be sold.

The goal isn't to upload videos forever. It's to beat each level, unlock the next skill, and eventually build a media business that runs without you.

00:00 YouTube automation is a video game
01:02 Level 1: You look like everybody else
03:50 Level 2: Your videos are fine and nobody clicks
06:08 Level 3: It's working and you are the bottleneck
08:30 Level 4: You hire people and it actually works
10:31 Level 5: The channel runs without you
11:57 Level 6: You own an asset, not a channel
13:08 Recap

snippet.description:
Join my FREE live YouTube workshop every Sunday:
https://aimediacompanies.com/r/claudecode

It took me just 15 videos to get my YouTube channel monetized. And the two videos that made it happen were created with Claude Code.

My student Gabriel followed a similar strategy and got monetized in 20 videos, generating €3,429 in his first two days. Today, his faceless channel makes between €5,000 and €8,000 per month.

In this video, I show you how to use Claude Code to find viral topics, research competitors, write scripts, generate AI voiceovers, edit videos, and create thumbnails without hiring an entire team.

I also walk you through connecting MCPs and AI tools like NexLev, ElevenLabs, and Higgsfield, finding YouTube outliers, and understanding what actually makes faceless channels grow.

This isn't about uploading random AI-generated videos. It's about finding proven demand, creating original content, and using AI to automate the repetitive work while you focus on growing your channel.

snippet.title: 10 Things You Should NEVER Do After Uploading A YouTube Video
snippet.description:
Join my FREE live YouTube workshop every Sunday:
https://aimediacompanies.com/r/10things

Most YouTube creators make their biggest mistakes AFTER uploading a video. And some of those mistakes can cost you thousands of views, delay monetization, or completely destroy your channel's growth.

In this video, I break down 10 things you should NEVER do after uploading a YouTube video, based on my experience building 14 channels, growing multiple channels past 1 million subscribers, and helping students build monetized faceless YouTube businesses.

We cover why you shouldn't publish videos before HD processing finishes, what happens when you send your videos to friends and group chats, why buying views can put your channel at risk, and why constantly changing thumbnails, deleting underperforming videos, or switching niches too early can hurt your progress.

I also explain how to properly analyze YouTube Studio, understand click-through rate (CTR) and average view duration (AVD), identify what's actually holding your videos back, and make better decisions before uploading your next video.

These are the mistakes I've made myself and watched hundreds of creators struggle with. Learning to avoid them can save you months of wasted work.

snippet.title: The YouTube Automation Bubble Is About To Burst
snippet.description:
DM me “YOUTUBE” on Instagram @arnas.st if you want to learn how to build faceless YouTube channels that actually work in 2026.

The YouTube automation bubble isn't about to burst. It already has. And most people still haven't realized what's happening.

For years, people have been selling the same business model: pick a niche, hire freelancers, generate videos with AI, and wait for passive income. But YouTube has changed, and mass-produced, repetitive content is no longer the easy money opportunity it once appeared to be.

In this video, I break down what happened to YouTube automation, why so many channels have stopped uploading, how YouTube's monetization policies are affecting creators, and why some gurus are still selling strategies they no longer use themselves.

I've personally built channels with millions of subscribers, generated hundreds of millions of views, and experienced what happens when successful channels get taken down.

I also explain the real costs of starting a faceless YouTube channel, why most beginners struggle, and the three stages of building a sustainable YouTube business: learning content creation, using AI to work smarter, and eventually hiring a team to scale.

Faceless YouTube isn't dead. The lazy, outdated version of automation is. And for creators who understand the new rules, there's still a massive opportunity.

snippet.title: How a 57-Year-Old Dad Makes $5,000/Month With Faceless YouTube
snippet.description:
At 57, with two kids and a business getting harder to run, Wayne needed a new option. This is his first year with faceless YouTube, unscripted.
Start here: https://youtubecashflow.com/r/wayne

Before joining my program, Wayne was running an Amazon FBA business full time from Canada. By his own account it had reached seven figures in sales, but tariffs, fees and inventory made it extremely capital intensive and the margins kept shrinking. He wanted something with low overhead, more flexibility, and the ability to build from behind a computer without being the face of a brand.

That is when he found faceless YouTube.

In this interview Wayne breaks down what life looked like before joining, why the no face model appealed to him, what doubts he had before starting, how he checked us out by messaging our students himself, and how he went from zero editing experience to several monetized channels.

We talk about the first month inside the program, the mistakes he made early on, how he learned editing, how AI helps him with scripts and voiceovers, why he stopped letting AI make the creative decisions, and why consistency mattered more than perfection.

Wayne also shares what it felt like when his first channel got monetized, how the first AdSense payout made it feel real, and where his channels are today. In his words, they now bring in around $5,000 a month combined, which gave him a real pivot away from Amazon FBA. He is also clear that he would not tell anyone to quit their job for this.

This is not a get rich overnight story. It is a case study of someone older, with a family, limited time and real responsibilities, building a new source of income online with about three hours a day.

If you think it is too late to start, this interview will probably change your mind.

Wayne's results are his own. They are not typical and not a promise. What he did is repeatable, what he got is not guaranteed.

snippet.title: Google Just Changed Faceless YouTube Forever
snippet.description:
DM me “YouTube” on Instagram @arnas.st if you want to learn how to keep building faceless YouTube channels even after Google’s new AI voiceover tracking update.

Google just changed the future of faceless YouTube, and a lot of creators are panicking.

Start working with us:
https://youtubecashflow.com/

With SynthID and AI voiceover tracking becoming more serious, many people now believe this could be the end of faceless channels, AI voiceovers, and automated content. In this video, I break down what this update actually means, why I don’t think you should panic, and what I’m personally doing with my own channels and students.

I talk about why you probably shouldn’t instantly switch away from ElevenLabs, why marking every video as altered content might not be the smartest move yet, and why the most important thing right now is to wait, observe, and understand how YouTube actually reacts.

The truth is, most viewers don’t care whether a video uses AI voiceover if the topic is relevant, interesting, and packaged well. In niches like celebrity news, sports drama, royal family gossip, or trending scandals, people are usually watching because they want the information — not because they care who recorded the voice.

I also explain why faceless YouTube is not dead, what could happen if YouTube starts labeling AI content, and what backup options creators still have if AI voiceovers ever become a real monetization problem.

If you’re building faceless channels, this update matters — but it doesn’t mean the model is over. It just means the game is changing again, and the creators who stay calm, adapt, and keep posting will have the advantage.

snippet.title: YouTube Just Revived a Forgotten Growth Hack ($200K Case Study)
snippet.description:
DM me “YOUTUBE” on Instagram @arnas.st if you want the exact live stream strategy I used to help scale a faceless YouTube channel past $200K.

YouTube just brought back one of the most underrated growth hacks I’ve ever used: live streams.

This feature helped me earn over $200,000 from faceless YouTube channels, and for years it felt completely dead. Nobody was really clicking live streams, they weren’t getting pushed on the homepage, and the RPM was usually worse than normal videos.

But now something changed.

In this video, I break down why YouTube live streams are suddenly getting recommended again, how I used them years ago on faceless gaming channels, and why this forgotten feature could be a massive opportunity for creators in 2025 and beyond.

I also share the exact live stream structure I tested, why running streams for too long can kill the monetization after publishing, and why the 12-hour mark matters. Some of my old live streams got over 500,000 views, and the majority of those views came after I clicked publish.

The most interesting part is that this is not only about live stream revenue. One of my students revived a dead channel using this method and made over $2,000 in just three days from live streams alone. Even better, those live streams started pushing his normal videos again too.

If you already have content uploaded on your channel, this might be one of the easiest growth experiments you can run. You can loop your existing videos, package the stream with a strong thumbnail, run it properly, and see if YouTube starts giving your channel a second life.

This is not complicated, but there are important details most people miss.

snippet.title: Instagram banned me 2 times in 30 days...
snippet.description:
Meta banned me twice in less than 30 days — and both times were for completely different reasons.

The first suspension was for “fraud and deception,” even though I wasn’t scamming anyone, running shady offers, or doing anything unusual. The second ban was for “account integrity,” where the platform basically treated me like a fake account or impersonator.

In this video, I explain the full story: what happened, what I tried, what actually worked, and what I learned after speaking with multiple insiders who deal with Instagram recoveries every day.

I also talk about why so many large pages are suddenly disappearing right now — including million-follower theme pages, coaching accounts, and creator brands. This isn’t just happening to small accounts anymore. Even established creators are getting hit by random ban waves.

I break down:
– why appealing too quickly can sometimes make recovery harder,
– how Meta’s current support system barely works anymore,
– why linking Facebook and Instagram together can become a nightmare if one account gets disabled,
– how insiders and recoveries actually work behind the scenes,
– and why relying only on Instagram for your business is becoming extremely dangerous.

I also share what I discovered about Meta Verified support, AI moderation, Telegram recovery markets, middlemen, and the strange patterns I noticed after both recoveries.

Most importantly, this video is not about “hacking” or bypassing anything. It’s about understanding how unstable modern platforms have become — and why creators need to diversify onto YouTube, Twitter/X, Telegram, Discord, email lists, and other platforms before losing everything overnight.

If you’re building an online business, personal brand, or audience in 2026, this is something you need to understand early.

snippet.title: Why Your YOUTUBE Videos Get 0 Views (Hidden Trust Score)
snippet.description:
Fill the form here if you want access to the exact strategies I use to fix low-view channels and scale faceless YouTube channels past $200K.

https://youtubecashflow.com/

If your YouTube videos are getting 0 views or barely any impressions, the problem might not be your editing, thumbnails, or niche. In this video I explain the concept of the hidden YouTube Trust Score and why many new channels struggle to get impressions even when the content quality is good.

A year ago I talked about this concept in my native language, and after analyzing over 100 faceless YouTube channels inside my BoostChannels community, I started noticing patterns between channels that blew up and channels that stayed stuck. Some channels had great watch time, strong engagement, and well-optimized scripts but still struggled to get reach. The reason often came down to channel trust signals connected to the Google account itself.

In this video I break down what I discovered after managing dozens of channels and working with creators who run faceless automation channels in different niches. I explain why aged Gmail accounts, profile details, account identity signals, and overall online presence can influence how YouTube initially treats your channel.

You’ll also learn practical steps that can help improve your channel’s credibility — from setting up your Google account properly, adding profile details and links, verifying your identity, building activity history online, and interacting with your audience through comments and community posts.

I also talk about how to recognize if your channel might be stuck in a low-trust state, what impressions data you should watch inside YouTube Studio, and when it might actually make sense to contact YouTube support if your videos never reach basic impression levels.

Another important part is understanding that persistence still matters. Some creators see almost no growth in the beginning, but once the algorithm gathers enough data and signals from your channel activity, impressions can suddenly start increasing.

If you’re building a faceless YouTube channel, understanding how YouTube evaluates new creators can make a huge difference in whether your videos stay invisible or start reaching thousands of viewers.

In this video, I explain how a new SEO-style update connected to Community Posts is helping channels explode in subscribers and impressions, sometimes without uploading a single video. One example I show grew to over 1 million subscribers using only posts — no long-form videos, no shorts, no livestreams.

If you’re uploading generic prank compilations, random comedy, or broad viral content, you’ll most likely attract tier 3 traffic like India or Bangladesh. When the topic is US-centric, the audience becomes US-centric. Simple.

I also explain why VPN tricks and fake setups can actually hurt you long-term. YouTube and Google track behavior patterns, IP consistency, account history, and audience signals. Trying to manipulate that can damage your channel’s trust. Instead, I show you the smarter approach: reverse-engineer 5 successful US-focused channels, study their titles, topics, structure, and angles — then recreate the idea in your own unique way.

You don’t need millions of views from random countries. 100,000 targeted US views can earn you more than 1,000,000 low-RPM views. That’s the game.
